related_questions.question: What are the guidelines for endometrial cancer?
related_questions.snippet: General treatment recommendations for endometrial cancer Endometrial cancer is treated primarily with surgery, including hysterectomy, bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy, abdominopelvic washings, and lymph node evaluation; advanced disease may be treated with maximal surgical cytoreduction.
related_questions.title: Endometrial Cancer Treatment Protocols - Medscape Reference

related_questions.question: Can you take estrogen if you had endometrial cancer?
related_questions.snippet: It is generally accepted that since survivors with early-stage endometrial cancer undergo hysterectomy and the cancer cells have not spread, the protective effect of progesterone on the endometrium can be disregarded in HT, and only estrogen is needed to relieve menopausal symptoms and bone protection.
related_questions.title: Hormone replacement therapy in endometrial cancer survivors

related_questions.question: What is the gold standard for endometrial cancer diagnosis?
related_questions.snippet: While an ultrasound is a helpful tool, the only way to diagnose endometrial cancer is through a biopsy.
related_questions.title: How Endometrial Cancer Is Diagnosed - Verywell Health

related_questions.question: What is the follow-up protocol for endometrial cancer?
related_questions.snippet: Experts recommend a physical exam every 3 to 6 months for the first 2 to 3 years, then every 6 or 12 months after that for up to 5 years, then every 12 months after that. Imaging tests should be done based on the physical exam and any changes the patient reports.
related_questions.title: Living as an Endometrial Cancer Survivor
